title: Experiment Safeguards Playbook: Thresholding, Observability & Escalation Milestones
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: define a prescriptive, minimally invasive playbook that product, engineering, and SRE teams will follow for any A/B test, canary, or phased rollout that could materially change inference latency, cost per token, or QA metrics. Goal is to reduce blast radius, speed decision-making on rollbacks/rollforwards, and provide clear escalation paths tied to OKRs (latency SLOs, cost-per-token targets, and quality regression allowances).
success_metrics: List of measurable outcomes we expect from adopting this playbook: 1) Mean time to detect a problematic experiment reduced to <10 minutes. 2) False-positive rollbacks <= 5% across first 6 weeks of rollouts. 3) 90% of experiments have annotated thresholds and monitoring before canary. 4) Product/PM-specified quality regressions detected by eval suite with precision >= 85%.
rollout_gates: Gate A - Pre-launch (checklist): canary cohort definition, chosen metrics (latency P95, error rate, cost/token, eval-precision), monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds, and runbook owner assigned. Gate B - Live canary (3-24 hour): automatic alerts for threshold breaches; human-in-loop approval if transient spike expires after grace window. Gate C - Gradual ramp: per-step limits (max X% traffic/day), automated rollback criteria, and rollback dry-run validated in staging. Gate D - Post-rollout (30d): quality regressions reviewed and metrics reconciled against OKRs.
milestones: 1) Draft playbook v0.1 and checklist (2026-03-12) - DONE. 2) Instrument standardized dashboards and create template alerts in Grafana/Datadog (2026-03-20) - In Progress (ENG-2412). 3) Add policy enforcement in console for required pre-launch artifacts (2026-03-25) - Planned (ENG-2578). 4) Run pilot on two low-risk feature flags and iterate (2026-03-28 to 2026-03-31) - Planned. 5) Ship playbook + template to org and link to PRD (2026-04-01) - Target.
stakeholder_feedback: Design review (DES-214): proposed dashboard must surface per-route token breakdown and include toggleable baseline; request to add colorblind-friendly palette. SRE input: require 'grace window' param for transient latency spikes; prefer 15-minute initial grace for noisy workloads. Legal: no new PI collected by experiment instrumentation. Product: ask that every experiment include a short plain-language customer-impact statement.
open_questions: 1) Should the console enforce gates or only surface advisory warnings? 2) What default canary cohort sizes balance signal vs. user risk for embeddings-heavy workloads? 3) Do we require a signed-off rollback owner for every experiment >P2?

acceptance_criteria: 1) Playbook documented in Confluence and linked from Console 'create experiment' flow. 2) Templates for dashboards and alert rules are checked into experimentation repo and usable by engineering teams. 3) Console shows advisory if required pre-launch artifacts are missing; enforcement optional behind a feature flag. 4) Pilot executed with two experiments; post-pilot retrospective recorded with actionable improvements. 5) OKR mapping updated: link experiments to growth/cost/quality objectives in tracking doc.

notes_for_reviewers: Please focus review on the proposed threshold heuristics for P95/P99 latency and the 'grace window' semantics. If you object to automation enforcing gates in console, add rationale and propose minimum viable enforcement. Add any missed metrics that should be required for an inference-related experiment (e.g., cost/token delta).
